prompt_en: An investigative-fiction photograph of a human investigator examining physical evidence. Use the supplied portrait as the visible face and hair appearance reference for the investigator, preserving the rounded face, dark brown eyes and chin-length dark bob with a wispy fringe. In the early-morning loading bay of a municipal archive, she is documenting a freshly cut security seal on a closed shipping crate while the receiving clerk steadies its trolley. This is the discovery that interrupts an ordinary delivery: a red plastic seal still threads the crate hasp, but its two cut ends part across a clear gap on the near face. A small numbered evidence marker rests beside that break. The crate fills the lower right of the horizontal frame, with the hasp and broken seal turned toward the viewer. The investigator stands to its left with both feet planted, leaning slightly from the hips. Her right hand holds a compact camera aimed down at the broken seal; her left gloved hand holds a short measuring scale flat against the crate immediately below the break, leaving the gap visible. Her gaze follows the camera toward that target, her lips slightly parted in quiet concentration. Her cheek and relaxed collar catch warm light, giving her an understated intimate presence within the absorbed work. A charcoal jacket and pale open-collar shirt have the lived-in creases of a long morning. The clerk stands beyond the trolley with both hands on its handle, looking down at the seal; his uneasy stillness makes clear that the shipment has stopped here. The trolley wheels remain on the concrete floor, the crate stable on its platform. A short run of scene cordon across the loading-bay entrance separates this inspection from the waiting delivery area. Shoot from the open side of the trolley at chest height with a moderate normal lens: the investigator's face, both working hands, camera, scale, hasp and separated seal ends share one readable plane. Give the seal enough image area to distinguish its two ends and their gap. Include the clerk and the trolley support in the same medium-wide photograph, with restrained depth separation. Cool morning light from the raised bay door meets a warmer work lamp over the crate, making the evidence clear while preserving the quiet interruption of work. The visible act is purposeful documentation of a damaged closure before the shipment moves.
